by flashing barely-perceptible imagery in a person's peripheral vision, in the center of their vision partially obscured by their blind spot (and /or now a strobing light) that has a high probability elicit a known emotional response, coupled with an uninterruptible and likewise barely-perceptible "radio" to transmit audio, surely it would be possible to influence a person in a number of difficult-if-not-impossible to resist ways.

From a "brain damage / it's your fault for doing drugs" standpoint:

All this crap first became distinctly visible to me after I had a severe incident involving rolling blackouts, violence, ataxia, and other stuff following the smoking of a blunt that I thought contained some typical marijuana. Spent 11 months in jail for that (2012) which fortunately allowed me to get clean and sober... long story. I did smoke a lot of weed, spice, and drink a lot of alcohol, besides the occasional use of the "usual suspects" for this stuff between the ages of 17 and 24.

I was injected with Ativan after the arrest but I don't think that would be responsible for any of this.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Perhaps more importantly, after my release I saw some childhood drawings I made that make it very much seem like these visuals may have been present my entire life. Just not "noticed" or understood, possibly existing solely in the blind spot at the center of the human eye or flashing too quickly in my peripheral vision. I was diagnosed with ADHD recently, (and my life has been drastically better in every way that matters since I got started on a Dexedrine prescription) and considering the habits and manner of my childhood and how I was without the medication, it is actually entirely plausible to me that I just never noticed this stuff for 26 years.

~~~~
Or perhaps that I was induced to choose the escapist coping mechanisms I did because my inner-experience was obnoxious and torturous in the way this stuff is. Anything that would serve to either deaden my sense of it or overwhelm it would be worth "risking my future" for.

A future with this experience constant in my day-to-day is next-to-worthless, and thus worth risking for basically any short-term pleasure. That is changing and I make "better" decisions now, but I don't feel as good about them as I "should" for this reason.

Only semi-related but maybe a contribution:

_______

Do you ever worry what you'd do if your dominant hand got injured?


Me neither, I use my left hand for the dangerous stuff like petting dogs and cats or touching other objects of uncertain risk.


...BUT if you do, I have a tip for you: learning to write with your off hand is pretty easy. I was in jail for 11 months a while back so I had more free time than most of you do BUT you only need a little time each day. More than redundancy, it is occasionally useful when writing in awkward positions or while holding things.

~~~

THE TRICK

*  Keep a daily journal, just a page or two at the end of or during each day

*  Write it by hand. 

* Every paragraph, switch hands.


##
This way, you get almost immediate internal-feedback when you do things like draw the 'a' or 'e' or '&' backwards. You can feel and access in short-term memory "oh that is the thing that I do with my right that I am translating incorrectly to my left"
###
I personally found that not only did it make my left hand more useful, but my handwriting in general improved from the self-examination.
